DECADEnts T6 - new heads, your changes, your keeps (2026-11-15)

26 pictures on HunyuanImage 3.0, numbered 1 to 26. Every control is optional. Tap what you want, press Copy answers, paste the line to jep. Click a picture to enlarge it.

Your ruling, 15 Nov: "We need to rethink some of the character concepts - I don't believe they'll ever look good. The 1940s, 1960s, 1980s, and 2000s. The 1920s sparked/inspired a new version of the idea: a porcelain statue wearing a porcelain mask - it's ridiculous and fits our nothing-human standard. The 1930s' two round eye-holes should always be black/reflective so that it'll fit our nothing-human standard. The 1950s toaster with the hat is funny. The 1970s all-sequins + white accent looks good. The 2010s is too feminine and the sunglasses are "real"/"3D" - it should be a blank yellow ball and everything is "drawn on it"."

Partial sheet: 26 of 46 pictures

The session's memory guard stopped the render around 12:44 with the PC critically low on memory (the image model held 12 GB, your open browser about 4 GB). jep stopped the image server and did not restart it. Rendered: all four heads for the 1940s, 1960s and 1980s, and one of four for the 2000s. Not rendered: three 2000s heads and all of Parts 2 and 3 (20 pictures, about 19 minutes). Their prompts are written and shown below in dashed boxes. They run on your word.

How this sheet was made, and what it showed

  1. Method: every new head is built from the four things you said you like (the toaster with the hat, all-sequins with white, a porcelain statue in a porcelain mask, a blank ball with a drawn face): one solid object from the decade, sized as a head, seated in the collar, with one joke stacked on it.
  2. All 23 prompts state the covering positively (long sleeves, gloves, closed collar). None contains a negation.
  3. 26 pictures on HunyuanImage 3.0, two per head, 54.5 to 67.5 seconds each (median 55.6).
  4. Two blind critics judged them at full size under shuffled file names and named each head before reading its brief. They named the intended object in 26 of 26. Head instruction followed fully: 22; partly: 4; not: 0.
  5. Nothing human visible anywhere: 12 of 26 clean, 6 uncertain, 8 with a clear leak. Every clear leak is costume, in two places: the open shirt collar under the 1980s heads (5) and a sleeve sliding down a raised arm (3). The fix is a closed collar and long gloves over the cuff; those re-renders are not done.
  6. Same critics, same scale, your four dropped concepts mixed in unmarked: mean look 2.8 and funny 2.2 of 5. The 26 new pictures: look 4.1, funny 4.0. Critics' scores, a pointer for where to look; the taps are yours.
  7. Open, by jep's eye: the 1940s pictures read as modern photographs with warm colour, short of a 1940s print. The radio's helmet came out in the German shape in both pictures; the next render names the helmet type.
